# Consul Logout

Command: `consul logout`

Corresponding HTTP API Endpoint: [\[POST\] /v1/acl/logout](/consul/api-docs/acl#logout-from-auth-method)

The `logout` command will destroy the provided token if it was created from
`consul login`.

If the token was created by an [OIDC auth method](/consul/docs/secure/acl/auth-method/oidc)
login and IdP logout is available, the command also prints the identity
provider logout URL so that you can end the provider session. Refer to
[OIDC logout](/consul/docs/secure/acl/auth-method/oidc#oidc-logout) for details.

The table below shows this command's [required ACLs](/consul/api-docs/api-structure#authentication). Configuration of
[blocking queries](/consul/api-docs/features/blocking) and [agent caching](/consul/api-docs/features/caching)
are not supported from commands, but may be from the corresponding HTTP endpoint.

| ACL Required |
| ------------ |
| `none`       |

## Usage

Usage: `consul logout [options]`

-> The token to delete should be specified with the `-token` argument, the
`CONSUL_HTTP_TOKEN` environment variable, the `-token-file` argument, or the
`CONSUL_HTTP_TOKEN_FILE` environment variable.

#### Command Options

- `-open-browser` - Also open the identity provider logout URL in your default
  browser. Applies only to tokens created by `consul login -type=oidc` when IdP
  logout is available. Consul always prints the URL. Do not use this option in
  non-interactive environments, such as CI pipelines. You can also set this
  option with the `CONSUL_LOGOUT_OPEN_BROWSER` environment variable. The flag
  takes precedence over the environment variable. Defaults to `false`.

#### API Options

@include 'legacy/http_api_options_client.mdx'

### Examples

Logout and delete a login token.

```shell-session
$ consul logout -token-file 'consul.token'
```

Logout, delete a login token created with an OIDC auth method, and open the
identity provider logout URL in your default browser.

```shell-session
$ consul logout -token-file 'consul.token' -open-browser
```
